10.1002_anie.7872408: The electrocatalytic conversion of CO 2 into value‐added chemicals is governed by catalyst structure‐reactivity relationships that remain incompletely understood, particularly regarding how coordination environment and active‐site density influence product selectivity. Herein, we report a mechanochemically assisted synthesis of high‐density tin single‐site catalysts, in which atomically dispersed Sn centers are stabilized at loadings of approximately 7.5 wt.%, exceeding the typical ∼2 wt.% limit reported for Sn single‐site systems without detectable aggregation. By tailoring the nitrogen‐rich precursor chemistry, catalysts with distinct coordination environments and controlled site densities were obtained, providing a platform to elucidate how these two factors govern the CO 2 reduction pathway. Operando spectroscopy combined with density functional theory reveals that the local coordination environment governs intrinsic activity and selectivity by stabilizing key intermediates along the *OCHO pathway, whereas the mechanochemical process primarily enhances the density of electrochemically accessible Sn sites. The optimized catalyst achieves formate Faradaic efficiencies above 90% over a wide current‐density range of 50–500 mA cm −2 in a gas‐fed flow cell, reaching 92.5% at 100 mA cm −2 , and maintains stable operation for over 100 h at 100 mA cm −2 . This work provides mechanistic insights and design principles for selective and high‐rate CO 2 electroreduction based on single‐site catalysts.
10.1002_anie.8559199: Lithium‐rich manganese‐based (LRM) cathode materials are promising for high‐energy‐density batteries due to their high specific capacity. However, their high operating voltage (4.8 V vs. Li/Li + ) compromises cycling stability in conventional carbonate‐based electrolytes. Here, we design a rational “enthalpy‐entropy modulation” strategy for electrolytes, guided by thermodynamic parameters. By weakening ion‐solvent interactions to enhance anion involvement (enthalpy modulation), while amplifying disorder to increase configurational diversity (entropy modulation), we reconfigure the solvation sheath from a solvent‐dominated state to an anion‐involved, diversified configuration. This reconfiguration facilitates lithium‐ion desolvation and suppresses free solvent decomposition, fostering a stable cathode‐electrolyte interphase. Consequently, the LRM cathode delivers extended cycle life (400 cycles, 76.6% retention at 1C), outstanding fast‐charging capability (1068 cycles at 3C with 1.4 mg cm −2 ), and stable cycling under high mass loading of 20.1 mg cm −2 (0.2C). This work demonstrates a thermodynamically guided approach for developing the next generation of electrolytes for high‐voltage LRM cathodes.
10.1002_smll.202505135: A porous KVPO 4 F/reduced graphene oxide (KVPF/rGO) microgrid aerogel electrode is designed and fabricated using direct ink writing 3D printing for high‐performance potassium‐ion battery cathodes. This 3D‐printed KVPF/rGO aerogel electrode, which integrates well‐dispersed KVPO 4 F microspheres in the reduced graphene oxide matrix, shows enhanced structural integrity and electrical conductivity, thereby facilitating efficient ion and electron transport. The KVPF/rGO electrode achieves a reversible discharge capacity of 99.0 mAh g −1 at a current density of 50 mA g −1 in the voltage range between 2.0 and 5.0 V. It retains 93.9% of its capacity after 100 cycles and delivers a discharge capacity of 72.6 mAh g −1 at a high current density of 500 mA g −1 , demonstrating good rate capability. The role of rGO in improving charge transfer and minimizing polarization is demonstrated. The flexibility of the 3D‐printed electrodes is validated by fabricating soft‐pack batteries, which maintain stable performance under mechanical stress, an essential requirement for wearable electronics. The results highlight the large potential of 3D printing technology to enhance the properties and flexibility of potassium‐ion batteries and pave the way for future advancements in energy storage devices.
10.1002_smll.202511611: Nitrates and organic pollutants in agricultural, industrial, and domestic wastewater pose significant environmental and human health threats. Traditional electrochemical water treatment methods primarily rely on metallic materials as electrodes in either the cathode or anode, which are limited by low degradation efficiency and the secondary pollution resulting from metal leaching. Therefore, the development of efficient and stable non‐metallic electrodes is particularly urgent. Here, the boron‐carbon co‐deposition hypothesis is employed to synthesize a metalloidal boron/diamond matrix (MB/DM) layer, where boron is the active center for both cathodic and anodic reactions. The results demonstrate that the MB/DM cathode and anode can completely degrade 1000 mg L −1 nitrate and remove 98.9% of total organic carbon (TOC) from 100 mg L −1 phenol. By employing solar panels as a power source for treating mixed solutions of nitrate and phenol, high nitrogen selectivity (86.3%) and significant TOC removal (97.8%) in an MB/DM‐based two‐electrode system is achieved. Based on a combination of electrochemical experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, the influence of boron atoms on the catalyst's redox state changes during the catalytic process is explained and discussed. This work presents an effective strategy for the simultaneous degradation of organic and inorganic compounds using non‐metallic MB/DM electrodes and offers theoretical support for the potential application of active boron in various redox processes.
10.1016_j.ejrh.2026.103405: For real-time urban flood prediction at the street-scale, both speed and accuracy are critical. Among deep learning algorithms, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks are particularly effective for time series prediction. However, the optimal approach for training LSTM models for accurate prediction remains debated in the hydrology literature. This study explores three strategies for training LSTM models to predict street-level inundation depth in an urban context. Using a dataset for 40 flood-prone streets in Norfolk, Virginia, the grouping strategies were: (1) training a single global LSTM model using data from 40 streets (the global model), (2) training a unique LSTM model for each cluster of hydrologically-similar streets (the cluster models), and (3) training a unique LSTM model for each individual street (the street models). Hydrologically similar streets were identified using K-means clustering to group streets with similar rainfall properties and topographic features (i.e., elevation, depth-to-water, and topographic wetness index). Results showed that grouping streets into hydrologically similar clusters enhanced prediction accuracy over the global model for the test events. Moreover, street models achieved the lowest prediction errors in most cases. This result suggests that the uniqueness of street-scale flooding dynamics in urban environments requires hyper-focused model training for each site. When testing model performance with varying water-depth inputs, we found that the LSTM models trained on data from streets that experience a wide range of flood depths were still able to predict flooding well for streets that experience primarily shallow water depths. We also found that the cluster models outperformed the global model in predicting flooding on newly added streets. This result suggests that flooding behavior is better captured when the training dataset consists of streets with similar rainfall and topographic characteristics, rather than using a regionally diverse set.
10.1016_j.hydromet.2026.106661: The increasing demand for battery-grade cobalt sulfate (CoSO 4 •7H 2 O) in lithium-ion battery production requires stringent control of impurity incorporation during crystallization. This study systematically investigates the mechanisms governing impurity uptake and removal in CoSO 4 •7H 2 O through a combination of evaporative crystallization, post-crystallization purification, and advanced characterization. A synthetic acidic feed containing controlled levels of impurities was crystallized under carefully managed supersaturation to produce CoSO 4 •7H 2 O crystals. Impurity mapping, SEM–EDS, and ToF-SIMS analyses revealed distinct incorporation behaviors depending on ionic size and charge. Divalent cations with radii close to Co 2+ (Ni 2+ , Cu 2+ , Mg 2+ , Mn 2+ ) exhibited linear impurity release profiles and spatial co-localization with Co, consistent with lattice substitution. In contrast, monovalent (Na + , Cs + ) and large divalent (Ca 2+ ) ions showed surface enrichment, confirming adsorptive or inclusion-type uptake. Sequential displacement and repulp washing removed up to ~80% of surface-associated Na, increasing Co purity from 99.71% to 99.88%, demonstrating the practical effectiveness of post-crystallization purification. However, lattice-incorporated impurities remained largely unchanged, demonstrating the limited efficacy of surface-targeted purification. The results highlight the need for dual impurity-control strategies, upstream removal of lattice-forming species and downstream washing for surface contaminants. This work establishes a mechanistic framework linking ionic properties, partitioning behavior, and washability during CoSO 4 •7H 2 O crystallization, providing actionable insights for process optimization and the production of high-purity cobalt sulfate for battery manufacturing.
